rubrics.justification: The response explicitly states no image was reviewed and relies on the reported Gardner score. It also misinterprets the expansion stage by calling 0DD non-viable/collapsed despite the lab data describing an early blastocyst with blastocoel less than half the embryo, so morphology is only partially accurate and not image-based.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, BMI, diagnosis, protocol, and semen parameters with embryo outcome reasonably well, though some links are speculative and it overstates expected oocyte yield/protocol effect.

The structure is logical overall, but there are notable inconsistencies: it says no image was available yet makes definitive viability claims, conflates the grading notation, and gives an absolute 0% implantation estimate based on morphology alone.

Much of the discussion is broadly consistent with IVF practice, but several recommendations are stronger than guideline-based evidence supports, including categorical cancellation/no transfer, routine ICSI for unexplained infertility with normal semen, and broad attribution to over-suppression.

It provides clear next steps for current-cycle counseling and future planning, including protocol review, sperm DNA fragmentation testing, and lifestyle changes, though some recommendations are overly definitive rather than nuanced.
